blogs.title: MRI-Negative Neuro-Behçet’s: Don’t Let a Normal Scan Fool You
blogs.description: Early acute neuro-Behçet’s can present as an aseptic meningitis with a normal MRI. This post walks through how to make the call when imaging is unrevealing: leaning on CSF (lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein), mucocutaneous criteria, and exclusion of infection and malignancy. We’ll outline a practical diagnostic algorithm, when to repeat imaging, and how to risk-stratify patients for close observation versus early immunomodulation.

blogs.title: Hyponatremia as a Signal: SIADH in Neuroinflammation and Behçet’s
blogs.description: SIADH can be the endocrine footprint of CNS inflammation in acute neuro-Behçet’s. We review the pathophysiology (IL-6–driven ADH release), the diagnostic framework for SIADH (hypotonic hyponatremia, inappropriately concentrated urine, euvolemia, normal thyroid/adrenal function), and the nuance that serum ADH levels are rarely needed. Management pearls include when fluid restriction suffices, when to consider hypertonic saline or vaptans, and how to avoid rapid correction.

blogs.title: Hiccups and Rhabdo from Salt Trouble: The Hyponatremia Clues You’ll Miss if You Don’t Look
blogs.description: Persistent hiccups and unexplained CK elevation can be sentinel clues to profound hyponatremia, including SIADH from neuroinflammation. We highlight when to check CK in hyponatremia, how to correct for hyperglycemia when interpreting sodium, and safe correction targets to prevent osmotic demyelination (including the role of a desmopressin clamp). A quick, bedside checklist translates these pearls into practice.

blogs.title: Colchicine-Only for Acute Neuro-Behçet’s? Steroid-Sparing Lessons from an N-of-1
blogs.description: Conventional teaching favors corticosteroids for acute neuro-Behçet’s, yet this case improved on colchicine monotherapy. We contrast guideline expectations with the literature on meningoencephalitis-predominant, MRI-negative presentations that may self-resolve, and propose a cautious, steroid-sparing pathway for selected mild cases (e.g., diabetes, limited deficits), with clear triggers to escalate to steroids or other immunosuppressants. Practical monitoring parameters and follow-up strategies are included.

blogs.title: Stop Shotgunning the Workup: Use Behçet’s Criteria and Pretest Probability
blogs.description: ACE and sIL-2R are low-yield screening tests without the right clinical context, and HLA-B51 is supportive but non-diagnostic. This post shows how to anchor the workup in the International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease, avoid indiscriminate testing, and still move fast on time-sensitive empiric antimicrobials while infectious etiologies are excluded. A streamlined diagnostic flow emphasizes clinical features over scattershot labs.

blogs.title: Two Diagnoses, One Visit: Catching Concurrent Behçet’s and Neuro-Behçet’s
blogs.description: Neuro-Behçet’s rarely debuts alongside first-time Behçet’s, which makes recognition easy to miss. We cover bedside heuristics to raise suspicion—new mucocutaneous lesions plus fever/headache, aseptic CSF findings, and otherwise unexplained hyponatremia—and how to distinguish common BD-associated headaches from true neuro-Behçet’s. The goal: don’t overcall, but don’t miss the minority who present with both.
